metadata.title: Master Chronology -- July 2, 1863 (Day 2)
metadata.tick_formula: Tick 226 = 5:00am July 2. Each tick = 5 minutes. Day 2 = ticks 226-450.
sources: Pfanz, Harry W. -- Gettysburg: The Second Day (UNC Press, 1987)
Pfanz, Harry W. -- Gettysburg: Culp's Hill and Cemetery Hill (UNC Press, 1993)
OR Vol. 27, Parts I and II
Hessler, James A. -- Sickles at Gettysburg (Savas Beatie, 2010)
Wert, Jeffry D. -- Gettysburg Day 3 (Simon and Schuster, 2001)

events.event: Both armies consolidate overnight positions. Lee reconnoiters the Union line from Seminary Ridge. Longstreet argues again for a strategic flanking movement. Lee overrules -- orders Longstreet to attack the Union left. The attack is to begin as early as possible.
events.narrative: Lee's decision to attack on July 2 rather than maneuver is the second most-debated Confederate command decision of the battle.

events.event: Sickles examines his assigned position on lower Cemetery Ridge and is dissatisfied. He believes the Peach Orchard ridge is higher ground and would be better. He begins to consider an unauthorized advance.

Longstreet's corps begins moving south for the flanking march. The march is complicated by the need to avoid Union observation from Little Round Top. Longstreet is slow and deliberate -- the controversial delay begins.

Berdan's sharpshooters (1st US Sharpshooters) sent into Pitzer's Woods by Sickles for reconnaissance. They find Wilcox's Confederate infantry. This confirms Confederate presence on Seminary Ridge south of town.
events.flag: Berdan Pitzer's Woods recon -- skirmish line advances into woods, fires on Confederates, withdraws. Skirmish Line disposition throughout.

events.event: Hood's division completes the flanking march and deploys south of Gettysburg. McLaws deploys north of Hood along Warfield Ridge. Alexander positions his artillery. The assault force is in position.
events.location: Warfield Ridge / south of Peach Orchard

events.event: Sickles advances his entire III Corps to the Peach Orchard -- without orders, without informing Meade, without permission. Creates a salient with an exposed apex at the Orchard and a dangerously thin line stretching to Devil's Den.
events.flag: Sickles's advance -- III Corps moves forward from Cemetery Ridge to Emmitsburg Road. This creates the tactical crisis of July 2. Show Line of March then Line of Battle deployment.
events.narrative: Sickles's unauthorized advance was tactically disastrous but may have drawn Confederate attention away from the Round Tops.

events.event: Meade discovers Sickles's unauthorized advance. Furious confrontation. Meade orders Sickles back -- but Confederate artillery has already opened fire and it is too late to withdraw without chaos.

LONGSTREET'S ASSAULT BEGINS. Alexander's Confederate artillery opens fire on the Peach Orchard salient -- 54 guns. Hood's division steps off in Line of Battle heading northeast toward Devil's Den and the Round Tops.
events.flag: Hood's assault begins. Four Confederate brigades in Line of Battle moving northeast. One of the largest single-corps assaults of the war.

events.event: Hood severely wounded -- arm permanently paralyzed by artillery fragment. Law assumes division command. Hood's request to swing around Big Round Top is denied by Longstreet.
events.flag: Hood wounded -- Law assumes division command. Commander succession CS-001 activates.

events.event: Law's brigade (formerly Hood's) reaches Big Round Top. 15th Alabama turns left and begins assaulting the southern slope of Little Round Top. Robertson's Texas Brigade engages Ward's Union brigade at Devil's Den and the Triangular Field.
events.location: Devil's Den / Little Round Top south slope

events.event: Little Round Top is UNOCCUPIED by Union infantry -- only a signal station on the summit. Warren, Meade's chief engineer, realizes the danger and desperately searches for troops to send there.
events.narrative: Warren's recognition of the Little Round Top crisis and his desperate improvisation to fill it was one of the most consequential individual decisions of the battle.

events.event: Warren intercepts Vincent's brigade (V Corps) on the march and diverts it to Little Round Top without waiting for formal orders. Vincent personally leads the brigade up the hill.

Vincent's brigade arrives on Little Round Top just ahead of Law's Confederates. Vincent places his regiments on the rocky slope: 16th Michigan right, 44th NY center, 83rd PA center-left, 20th Maine on the extreme left.
events.flag: Vincent's brigade deploys on Little Round Top. 20th Maine placed on the extreme left with REFUSED FLANK.

events.event: 15th Alabama (Oates) makes its first assault on 20th Maine's refused left flank. Chamberlain's line bends but holds. Multiple Confederate assaults follow over the next 30-40 minutes.
events.flag: 15th AL vs 20th ME -- first assault. Multiple assaults required across ticks 268-275. C-15AL shows repeated Charging Line disposition.

events.event: Vincent mortally wounded on Little Round Top. Rice assumes brigade command. Weed's brigade arrives on the summit. Hazlett drags guns up the steep rocky slope. O'Rorke's 140th NY arrives at the summit.
events.flag: Vincent falls. Weed and Hazlett on summit. O'Rorke arrives. Commander succession US-015 activates.

events.event: O'Rorke charges downhill without waiting for orders -- 140th NY sweeps Confederates off the northern slope of Little Round Top. O'Rorke shot through the neck and killed instantly.
events.flag: O'Rorke's charge -- regiment arrives at summit then immediately charges downhill. KIA at bottom.

events.event: Weed killed on the summit. Hazlett shot kneeling beside the dying Weed. Both general and artillery commander die almost simultaneously. Rittenhouse assumes battery command.
events.flag: Weed and Hazlett killed together. Commander successions US-016 and US-024 activate.

events.event: 16th Michigan on Vincent's right begins to waver -- brief near-break. The regiment steadies before the line collapses. Critical moment.
events.flag: 16th MI near-break. Show Chaotic Retreat disposition for 1-2 ticks before returning to Line of Battle.

events.event: CHAMBERLAIN'S BAYONET CHARGE. 20th Maine has expended nearly all ammunition after repulsing multiple assaults. Chamberlain orders a bayonet charge -- right-wheel motion sweeping down the hill. 15th Alabama broken and retreating. Nearly 400 Confederate prisoners.
events.flag: Chamberlain's charge -- 20th ME changes from Line of Battle (refused) to Charging Line sweeping downhill. C-15AL shows Chaotic Retreat. Most famous regimental combat of the battle.

events.event: McLaws's assault begins. Barksdale's Mississippi brigade charges the Peach Orchard in one of the most dramatic charges of the battle. Barksdale rides ahead of his men on horseback.
events.flag: Barksdale's charge. Brigade in Charging Line disposition attacking northeast. Barksdale rides ahead -- mortally wounded soon after. Graham wounded and captured.

events.event: Peach Orchard salient collapses. Graham wounded and captured. 141st PA suffers 71% casualties at the apex. III Corps line crumbling from the south toward Cemetery Ridge.
events.flag: Sickles wounded -- leg amputated (tick ~298). Commander succession US-017 activates.

events.event: Kershaw's South Carolina brigade engages in Rose Woods and the Wheatfield. DeTrobriand's Union brigade holds initially. G.T. Anderson's Georgia brigade pressing from the south.
Caldwell's II Corps division rushed south to reinforce the collapsing III Corps. Four brigades -- Cross, Kelly (Irish Brigade), Zook, Brooke -- advance into the Wheatfield.
events.narrative: Father Corby administers general absolution to the Irish Brigade before the charge. A kneeling army watches from Cemetery Ridge.

events.event: Father Corby's absolution. The Irish Brigade kneels in the field to receive general absolution before charging into the Wheatfield. One of the most dramatic religious moments of the war.
events.narrative: Corby stood on a rock and gave absolution -- all nearby troops of any faith knelt or bowed their heads.

events.event: Cross killed entering the Wheatfield. Zook mortally wounded. Brooke's brigade pushes farthest into the Wheatfield of any Union brigade. Semmes's Confederates mortally wounded.
events.flag: Cross KIA tick 290. Zook KIA tick 293. Commander successions US-009 and US-010 activate.

events.event: Wofford's fresh Georgia brigade sweeps through the Wheatfield behind the retreating Caldwell -- reaches the farthest Confederate penetration toward Cemetery Ridge. Tilton's controversial withdrawal exposed the Union flank.
events.flag: Wofford's advance -- show brigade reaching closest point to Cemetery Ridge before Crawford's charge drives them back.

events.event: Crawford's Pennsylvania Reserves charge down the western slope of Little Round Top -- drives Wofford's exhausted Confederates back through the Wheatfield. Colonel Taylor of 13th PA Reserves killed. Caldwell's position partially restored.
events.location: Wheatfield / Little Round Top west slope
events.flag: Crawford's charge downhill -- show brigade in Charging Line descending from Little Round Top area.

events.event: SICKLES WOUNDED. Artillery shell shatters Sickles's right leg near the Trostle Farm. Sickles famously smokes a cigar as he is carried from the field. Birney assumes III Corps command. Commander succession US-017 activates.
events.flag: Sickles wounded. Commander succession activates.

events.event: McGilvery's emergency artillery line. McGilvery assembles guns from multiple batteries -- Bigelow, Phillips, Hart -- along Plum Run to plug the gap left by III Corps collapse. Bigelow's battery ordered to hold without support.
events.flag: McGilvery's Plum Run Line. Bigelow's withdrawal from Trostle Farm begins.

events.event: BIGELOW'S TROSTLE FARM WITHDRAWAL. Bigelow's 9th Massachusetts battery ordered to hold as long as possible to buy time for McGilvery. Battery fights by prolonge (rope), losing guns one by one. Heroic withdrawal saves McGilvery's line.
events.flag: Bigelow's withdrawal -- battery must show multiple disposition changes: Deployed, withdrawing by section, losing a gun, final stand at Trostle Farm wall. 4-5 ticks of precise movement.

events.event: 1ST MINNESOTA'S CHARGE. Cemetery Ridge gap is open. Wilcox's Confederate brigade advancing toward the gap. Hancock has nothing to send but Colvill's 262-man 1st Minnesota. 'My God, are these all the men we have?' Orders them to charge Wilcox's entire brigade to buy 5 minutes.
events.flag: 1st Minnesota charge -- regiment advances from Cemetery Ridge toward Wilcox near Plum Run. CRITICAL ANIMATION. Tick 302. 224 of 262 men fall in approximately 15 minutes.

events.event: 1st Minnesota engages Wilcox's Confederate brigade. Both flanks overlapped but the charge stops Wilcox long enough for reinforcements to arrive. Colvill wounded, Messick killed, Coates assumes command. 85.5% casualties.
events.flag: 1st MN at maximum casualties -- show dramatic strength reduction. C-III-1-1 halted and then repulsed.

events.event: Wilcox's advance halted. Reinforcements close the gap on Cemetery Ridge. Wright's Georgia brigade briefly breaks through Cemetery Ridge north of Wilcox but is driven back without support.
events.flag: Wright's brief breakthrough at Cemetery Ridge. Brigade reaches crest for 1-2 ticks before being driven back.

events.event: Stuart arrives with his cavalry after controversial absence. Lee reportedly greets him: 'General Stuart, where have you been?' Confederate cavalry now available for the first time since before the campaign began. Commander succession CS-016 activates.

Johnson's Confederate division advances on Culp's Hill at dusk. XII Corps has been stripped away to reinforce Cemetery Ridge leaving only Greene's brigade (1,424 men) to hold the entire hill against 6,500 Confederates.
events.narrative: Greene's lone stand is one of the finest defensive performances of the war -- 1,424 men holding against 6,500.

events.event: GREENE'S LONE STAND. Greene's brigade holds Culp's Hill alone. Johnson's Confederates (Stonewall Brigade, Jones, Nicholls, Steuart) assault repeatedly. Greene extends his thin line and bends but never breaks.
events.flag: Greene's lone stand. Show thin Union line holding against multiple Confederate brigades. Steuart's brigade achieves deepest penetration into empty Union works.

events.event: Steuart's Confederate brigade occupies vacant XII Corps breastworks on lower Culp's Hill -- the right of the Union position. XII Corps (returning from Cemetery Ridge) finds their own works occupied by Confederates.
events.flag: Steuart occupies Union works. Confederate brigade shows Line of Battle in Union breastwork positions.

events.event: XII Corps returns to Culp's Hill and finds Confederate troops in their works. Night attack repossesses most of the upper works. Lower works remain Confederate. Sets up the July 3 morning fight.
CEMETERY HILL ASSAULT. Hays's Louisiana Tigers and Avery's North Carolina brigade charge Cemetery Hill at dusk. They reach the crest and briefly seize Union guns.
events.flag: Cemetery Hill assault -- Hays and Avery advance up the hill. Temporarily occupy crest for 1-2 ticks. Then driven back by Carroll's brigade. Show Charging Line then brief occupation then Chaotic Retreat.

events.event: Avery mortally wounded on the slope of Cemetery Hill writing his blood message: 'Tell my father I died with my face to the enemy.' Godwin assumes brigade command. Commander succession CS-014 activates.
events.flag: Avery's blood message. Mortally wounded. CS-014 commander succession activates.

events.event: Carroll's Union brigade counterattacks Cemetery Hill -- drives Louisiana Tigers and Avery's brigade back down the slope. Cemetery Hill secure. The last Confederate attempt to take the Union center ends.

Willard's brigade (II Corps -- 'Harper's Ferry Cowards' seeking redemption) charges Barksdale's exhausted Confederates near Plum Run. Willard killed by artillery shell. Barksdale mortally wounded nearby. Both commanders fall almost simultaneously.
events.flag: Willard KIA. Barksdale mortally wounded. Commander successions US-013 (Willard) and CS-003 (Barksdale) activate.

events.event: Fighting dies down across the battlefield. Both sides hold approximately their morning positions except: Confederates hold lower Culp's Hill works. Union line on Cemetery Ridge is intact. III Corps is shattered. The enormous cost of July 2 becomes clear.
events.narrative: July 2 was the bloodiest single day of the Gettysburg campaign -- approximately 20,000 total casualties across both armies.

events.event: Lee and Longstreet meet. Lee decides to attack Cemetery Ridge with Pickett's fresh division plus Pettigrew and Trimble July 3. Longstreet argues against it: 'General, I have been a soldier all my life... it is my opinion that no 15,000 men ever arrayed for battle can take that position.' Lee overrules.
events.narrative: This exchange -- Longstreet's most famous protest -- became the center of the Lost Cause argument that Longstreet lost Gettysburg. Most historians side with Longstreet's assessment.

events.event: Alexander begins positioning Confederate artillery along Seminary Ridge for the July 3 cannonade. Approximately 170 guns will fire tomorrow. The ammunition situation is already tight.
Meade holds council of war. All corps commanders polled -- decision is unanimous to remain and fight on July 3. Meade predicts Lee will attack his center. He is correct.
events.narrative: Meade's prediction that Lee would attack his center on July 3 is one of the most accurate command predictions of the war.

events.event: Both armies settle in for the night. Pickett's division -- fresh, not yet engaged -- moves into position behind Seminary Ridge. Pettigrew's and Trimble's commands positioned on Seminary Ridge left.
Johnson's Confederates dig in on lower Culp's Hill. XII Corps prepares for the morning counterattack. Meade orders artillery chief Hunt to conserve ammunition -- critical decision for July 3.

End of Day 2. Tallying casualties: approximately 10,000 Union, 10,000 Confederate. III Corps effectively destroyed as a fighting force. Both Round Tops firmly in Union hands. Cemetery Hill and Culp's Hill (mostly) held. Lee will attack the center tomorrow.
